finding: forms is isolated because it is UNFINISHED, never because wiring was removed: its only React surface, FormSettingsSection, has never had a consumer in the repo's history, so no user has ever reached the module.
evidence: src/shared/forms/FormSettingsSection.tsx is exported only by the barrel src/shared/forms/index.ts:16 and imported by nothing else (grep across src/ + demo/ returns only that barrel line and its own tests). `git log --all -S "useFormHandler"` shows the only historical touches are 7-line redirect shims in the deleted src/components/forms/ graveyard (commit 3f17e66c8, `.../components/forms/FormSettingsSection.tsx | 7 -`), i.e. shims, not a live mount. The inspector has no form section at all: grep -rln "formConfig|FormSettings" src/editor/inspector/ returns nothing.
fix: Either mount FormSettingsSection as an inspector section for elementType 'form' (registry pattern: src/editor/inspector/sections/registry/effects.tsx:79), or delete engine/forms/ + shared/forms/FormSettingsSection.tsx + shared/hooks/useFormHandler.ts and keep only the server FormBlock path.
chain: forms -> FormConfig -> configure a form -> (no trigger: no mounted surface) -> inspector -> user cannot set an action, webhook, success message or redirect on any form

finding: The published-site form wiring is unreachable, correcting the assumption that a published form may work while the editor is unaware: FormspreeInjector only fires when element.data.formConfig exists, and that key has exactly one writer in the whole repo — the unmounted FormSettingsSection.
evidence: ExportEngine.ts:899 gates on `element.type === "form" && element.data?.formConfig`; ExportEngine.ts:918 and :928 build the formspree/custom FormSettings. grep -rn "formConfig" src (excluding tests) returns writers at FormSettingsSection.tsx:45 and :64 only — every other hit is a read in ExportEngine. FormsScreen's own walked note says the same: "the settings section that would set one (shared/forms/FormSettingsSection) has no consumer, so a user cannot reach it either" (FormsScreen.emptyCopy.test.ts:11-13).
fix: Mount the settings section (MOD-D-01). Until then FormspreeInjector, its 153 lines and its test file are provably dead in production.
chain: forms -> FormConfig.webhookUrl -> set a Formspree/custom endpoint -> (no writer reachable) -> engine/export FormspreeInjector -> every published form ships with no action attribute and posts nowhere

finding: Nothing forms owns survives a reload. FormConfig, FormState and FormFieldDef live in three private Maps on FormHandler, and submissions live in a private Map on FormSubmissionService — none of them appear in ProjectData.
evidence: FormHandler.ts:104-106 declares `forms`, `formStates`, `formFields` as `Map`. FormSubmissionService.ts:99 `private submissions: Map<string, FormSubmission[]>`; :120-122 pushes into it; :148-150 `getSubmissions` reads it back. ProjectData (shared/types/project.ts:30-49) carries version/pages/pagesOrder/styles/assets/metadata/settings/dsSchemaVersion and no forms field. The only durable half is FormConfig mirrored onto the element as `data.formConfig` (FormSettingsSection.tsx:45), which rides the page tree — and that writer is unmounted.
fix: Persist FormConfig only on the element (already the export contract) and delete FormHandler's parallel registry; route submissions to the server FormSubmission rows the Settings inbox already reads.
chain: forms -> FormSubmission -> submit a form in the editor -> reload -> (nothing) -> the submission is gone, and getSubmissions returns an empty array for a form that had rows a second ago

finding: There are three unconnected form systems, and the one with a UI is fed by none of the other two: the Settings inbox reads server Prisma rows, the engine writes to an in-memory Map, and the exporter reads element data.
evidence: (1) FormsScreen.tsx:87 `forms.listBlocks.query({siteId})` and :112 `forms.listSubmissions.query(...)` over tRPC. (2) FormHandler.ts:268 `this.submissionService.submit(...)` into the in-process Map. (3) ExportEngine.ts:878-881 `collectFormElements` + `formspreeInjector.processHTML`. No code path connects (2) or (3) to (1); FormsScreen's empty state says so in prose: "nothing creates a FormBlock row except site duplication" (FormsScreen.tsx:243-244).
fix: Pick one owner. The server rows are the only durable one — make the exporter emit an action pointing at /api/public/forms/[siteId]/[blockId] and create the FormBlock row when a Form block is inserted.
chain: forms -> FormSubmission -> a visitor submits a published form -> (no action attribute, no FormBlock row) -> Settings · Forms inbox -> the inbox can only ever render 'No forms yet'

finding: All 7 FORM_* events emit onto the shared composer bus and reach only one listener set, which is itself unmounted and does nothing when called.
evidence: FormHandler emits FORM_REGISTERED (:125), FORM_UNREGISTERED (:136), FORM_UPDATED (:153), FORM_RESET (:231), FORM_SUBMITTING (:254), FORM_SUBMITTED (:302), FORM_ERROR (:304,:325) via `this.composer.emit`. The only subscriber is useFormHandler.ts:38-41, whose handler body is `const handleFormEvent = () => { /* Force re-render to get updated form states */ }` (:34-36) — an empty function that re-renders nothing — and its only caller is the unmounted FormSettingsSection.tsx:32.
fix: On FORM_SUBMITTED, a toast + the Settings inbox badge should update; on FORM_ERROR, the canvas form element should show its configured errorMessage. Give the events real listeners or delete them from events.ts.
chain: forms -> FormState -> submitForm() succeeds -> FORM_SUBMITTED -> editor/shell toasts + Settings·Forms inbox -> no confirmation anywhere; the user cannot tell a submit from a no-op

finding: FormConfig.action = 'email' and every emailOptions field are dead branches: no editor surface writes settings.integrations.email, which is the only thing that configures the two email services.
evidence: Composer.ts:749 `emailMarketingService.configure(emailConfig)` and :755/:766 `emailService.configure(...)` all read `this.projectSettings.integrations?.email`. grep -rn "integrations.email|EmailServiceConfig|emailConfig" src/editor returns nothing; IntegrationsScreen.tsx and IntegrationsHub.tsx contain no email/mailchimp/sendgrid string. So `emailService.isConfigured()` (EmailService.ts:198-200) is always false and FormSubmissionService.ts:130 never runs; the same for emailMarketingService.isConfigured() at FormHandler.ts:275.
fix: Add the email-integration fields to Settings · Integrations, or drop the 'Send Email' action from the FormConfig union and the subscribeToList branch.
chain: forms -> FormConfig.action='email' -> user picks 'Send Email' -> settings.integrations.email -> services/EmailService -> nothing is ever sent and no error is shown, because the guard returns silently

finding: FormStateOverlay — the only surface that renders isSubmitting / isSubmitted / errors to a user — is also unmounted, so the FormState entity has no reader at all.
evidence: src/shared/forms/FormStateOverlay.tsx exists and imports `FormState` from engine/forms/FormHandler (:8); it is exported at shared/forms/index.ts:15 and imported by nothing outside its own test. FormState is produced at FormHandler.ts:253, :290-298 and :318-323 and consumed by no live code.
fix: Mount it inside the canvas form element while a submit is in flight, or delete it with the rest of the unwired forms surface.
chain: forms -> FormState.isSubmitting -> submitForm() sets it -> (no reader) -> canvas -> a form gives no pending, success or error feedback while submitting

finding: FormSettingsSection is built entirely outside the design system — 5 raw <select>/<input> elements and 7 inline CSSProperties style objects — so it would fail Gate 24 the moment anyone mounted it.
evidence: FormSettingsSection.tsx:104-112 raw `<select>`, :118-124, :130-136, :141-147, :152-158, :163-169 raw `<input>`; styles at :180-234 are inline objects (`sectionStyles`, `headerStyles`, `fieldStyles`, `labelStyles`, `valueStyles`, `inputStyles`, `selectStyles`, `hintStyles`). CLAUDE.md §CI gates: Gate 24 — zero inline <button>/<input>/<select>/<textarea> in chrome, chrome-ui/ is the only exempt owner.
fix: Rebuild on @/editor/chrome-ui TextInput/Select before mounting; the file predates the flowbite migration and was never swept because the sweep followed imports.
chain: forms -> FormConfig -> configure a form -> mount FormSettingsSection -> Gate 24 -> the mount that fixes MOD-D-01 fails the pre-push gate unless the file is rebuilt first

finding: Already filed, not re-filed: the Settings · Forms PROVIDER card (provider / endpoint URL / spam protection) has no home in the repo — see W-B-27. Adding the module's view: the nearest code home IS FormConfig.webhookUrl on a per-element surface, and that surface is unmounted, so the card has no home on either the site or the element level.
evidence: W-B-27 (findings/W-B.jsonl, board 640:3135, Critical). Confirmed independently: the provider union is a dead type at shared/types/seo.ts:15 (`provider: "formspree" | "custom"`), read only by FormspreeInjector.ts:39,54 and written only by ExportEngine.ts:918,928 from webhookUrl string-matching (`formConfig.webhookUrl.includes("formspree.io")`, :910) — nobody ever sets `provider` directly.
fix: Resolve W-B-27 first (site-level vs per-element). If per-element, the fix is MOD-D-01 plus a provider select instead of URL sniffing.
chain: forms -> FormSettings.provider -> choose a form provider -> (drawn on 640:3135, no field anywhere) -> engine/export FormspreeInjector -> provider is inferred by substring-matching a URL the user cannot enter

finding: interactions looks isolated in the event graph but is NOT isolated in code — the inspector reads and writes the same storage slot through a completely different API, so the module is bypassed, not disconnected. Two writers exist for element.data.data.interactions and the live one is not InteractionManager.
evidence: Writer A: InteractionManager.setInteractions (InteractionManager.ts:258-265) sets `data.data.interactions` + `composer.markDirty()`, emits INTERACTION_*. Writer B: ElementOperations.setInteractions (ElementOperations.ts:250-258) sets the identical slot, emits ELEMENT_UPDATED + markDirty. The inspector uses B: registry/effects.tsx:100 `el.setInteractions?.(interactions)` inside `beginTransaction("interactions-change")` (:97), and reads via `el.getInteractions()` (:91). grep for addInteraction/updateInteraction/removeInteraction/toggleInteraction/reorderInteraction across src/ returns no call on composer.canvas.interactions outside engine/interactions/ and its tests.
fix: Delete InteractionManager's CRUD half (it is semantic duplication under CLAUDE.md §3) and keep only startRuntime/stopRuntime, or re-point registry/effects.tsx at composer.canvas.interactions and delete ElementOperations' copy. One slot, one writer.
chain: interactions -> Interaction[] -> add/edit/remove an interaction in the inspector -> ElementOperations.setInteractions -> (InteractionManager bypassed) -> all 6 INTERACTION_* CRUD events are unreachable from any user action

finding: The editor-side interaction runtime is unreachable: startRuntime() has exactly one call site, inside Composer.setPreviewMode(), and setPreviewMode has ZERO callers in the entire repo — its former caller was deliberately re-pointed.
evidence: Composer.ts:1088 `this.canvas.interactions.startRuntime()` / :1090 stopRuntime, both inside `setPreviewMode` (:1082). `grep -rn "setPreviewMode(" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx packages/editor/src packages/editor/demo packages/editor/e2e packages/dashboard/app packages/dashboard/components` returns exactly one line: the definition at Composer.ts:1082. The removal is documented: "UI_TOGGLE_PREVIEW used to flip composer.setPreviewMode here… The engine method is left alone: it drives InteractionManager's runtime" (useEditorEventListeners.ts:176-182) and AquibraStudio.tsx:189-197, from commit 57bef459f.
fix: Either call startRuntime() when the canvas mounts so interactions play live on the canvas, or delete InteractionRuntime.ts (531 lines), setPreviewMode, isPreviewMode, state.isPreviewMode and EVENTS.PREVIEW_MODE_CHANGED together.
chain: interactions -> InteractionRuntime -> author a hover/click interaction -> startRuntime() (no caller) -> editor/canvas -> nothing animates on the canvas itself; the interaction is only observable in the Preview overlay's exported document

finding: GSAP is bundled into the editor to serve dead code. Its only importer is GSAPEngine, whose only behavioural consumer is the unreachable InteractionRuntime; the one live import of GSAPEngine takes a static string map.
evidence: GSAPEngine.ts:9 `import { gsap } from "gsap"` is the sole gsap import in src/ (grep). Its consumers: InteractionRuntime.ts:10 `import { gsapEngine, type TimelineStep }` (used at :318) — unreachable per MOD-D-11 — and editor/inspector/sections/interactions/types.ts:6 which imports `GSAPEngine` only to build `EASING_OPTIONS = Object.entries(GSAPEngine.EASINGS)` (:159-162). animations/index.ts:4 states the assumption that is now false: "Only GSAPEngine remains (live consumer: InteractionRuntime)."
fix: Move EASINGS to shared/constants and drop the gsap dependency with InteractionRuntime, or wire the runtime (MOD-D-11) so the dependency earns its weight.
chain: interactions -> InteractionAnimationConfig.easing -> populate the easing dropdown -> GSAPEngine.EASINGS -> gsap package -> the whole GSAP library ships in the editor bundle to supply a ten-entry string→string map

finding: Three separate implementations of the same preset catalogue exist and a live test pins the DEAD one as a source of truth, so the module nobody runs is the module the suite protects hardest.
evidence: presetCoverage.test.ts:14 imports `PRESET_TIMELINES` from @/engine/interactions/InteractionRuntime and asserts `expect(PRESET_TIMELINES[preset]).toBeDefined()` for every offered preset (:29-31) — over the unreachable runtime. The same file also checks ANIMATION_KEYFRAMES (:54-56) and INTERACTION_PRESET_KEYFRAMES (:62-66), and its own comment names the third as "the only one a PUBLISHED page runs" (:57-58). A second parity file, interactionRuntime.triggerParity.test.ts:4-7, records a divergence that already shipped: 'While Pressed' worked in the editor runtime and did nothing for a visitor.
fix: Collapse to one catalogue. If InteractionRuntime is deleted (MOD-D-11), move PRESET_TIMELINES' data into shared/constants and re-point the test.
chain: interactions -> InteractionAnimationConfig.preset -> pick an animation preset -> three catalogues (PRESET_TIMELINES, ANIMATION_KEYFRAMES, INTERACTION_PRESET_KEYFRAMES) -> canvas + preview + published page -> a preset can be present in one and absent in another, which has shipped twice (20 missing keyframes, 22 missing published presets)

finding: The inspector's Preview button ignores the interaction's trigger entirely — it plays the animation once on click no matter what the trigger is, so 13 of the 14 triggers cannot be checked before publishing.
evidence: registry/effects.tsx:105-116 `handleInteractionPreview` reads only `interaction.animation` and sets `domEl.style.animation = \`bd-anim-${anim.preset} ${anim.duration}ms ${anim.easing} ${anim.delay}ms 1 normal forwards\`` — `interaction.trigger` is never read. The inspector offers 14 triggers (triggerParity.test.ts:23 asserts `expect(offered).toHaveLength(14)`).
fix: Route Preview through the runtime (start it for the selected element only) so scroll-into-view, while-pressed, page-load etc. can be exercised in place.
chain: interactions -> Interaction.trigger -> press Preview on a 'Scroll into view' interaction -> handleInteractionPreview (trigger discarded) -> canvas -> the animation fires immediately on click, which is the one thing the configured trigger does not do

finding: INTERACTIONS_RUNTIME_STARTED / _STOPPED and PREVIEW_MODE_CHANGED are emitted by an unreachable method, so three events can never fire at all — they are not orphans-with-no-listener, they are orphans-with-no-emitter-in-practice.
evidence: InteractionManager.ts:51 emits INTERACTIONS_RUNTIME_STARTED and :57 INTERACTIONS_RUNTIME_STOPPED, both only inside startRuntime/stopRuntime; Composer.ts:1093 emits PREVIEW_MODE_CHANGED inside setPreviewMode. All three sit behind setPreviewMode, which has no caller (MOD-D-11). AquibraStudio.tsx:194-196 records the same: PREVIEW_MODE_CHANGED "(nothing listens) and changes not one pixel of chrome".
fix: Delete all three constants when InteractionRuntime goes, or make the canvas chrome (cursor, overlay suppression, rail dimming) subscribe once the runtime is wired.
chain: interactions -> runtime lifecycle -> enter preview -> INTERACTIONS_RUNTIME_STARTED -> editor/canvas overlays -> selection rings, badges and guides stay drawn over a 'preview' that never starts

finding: Interactions DO survive a reload — they ride the page tree as element custom data — but only via the ElementOperations writer; the InteractionManager writer would lose them from history because it never opens a transaction.
evidence: Storage slot is `element.data.data.interactions`, and ElementData carries `data?: Record<string, unknown>` (shared/types/element.ts:76), which serializes with pages inside ProjectData.pages (shared/types/project.ts:34). Live writer registry/effects.tsx:97-102 wraps in `beginTransaction("interactions-change")` / `endTransaction()`. InteractionManager.setInteractions (:258-265) calls only `markDirty()` — no transaction and no ELEMENT_UPDATED, so a write through it would neither be undoable as one step nor repaint the canvas.
fix: If MOD-D-10 is resolved toward InteractionManager, add the transaction and the ELEMENT_UPDATED emit before re-pointing any caller.
chain: interactions -> Interaction[] -> add an interaction via InteractionManager -> markDirty() only -> engine/HistoryManager + canvas -> the change is not one undo step and the canvas does not repaint

finding: Already filed, not re-filed: W-I-25 (INTERACTIONS and ANIMATION collapsed on every inspector profile board, open on none) and W-O-03 (the interaction-test screen is an orphan with no inbound control). Adding the module's view: the missing board matters more than a normal collapsed section, because the panel is the ONLY place interactions can be authored at all.
evidence: W-I-25 (findings/W-I.jsonl, Major); W-O-03 (findings/W-O.jsonl, Major). Independently: the section is the sole authoring surface — inspector/sections/interactions/index.tsx:45 is the only component that constructs an Interaction (:57-63), reached through registry/effects.tsx:79.
fix: Draw the open INTERACTIONS section, its Add-Interaction panel and its per-interaction editor as boards; they carry a 14-trigger picker and a 39-preset picker that exist nowhere in the design file.
chain: interactions -> Interaction -> add an interaction -> the inspector's Interactions section (drawn only collapsed) -> Figma page 1:3 -> the only authoring surface for the feature is undrawn, so nobody can review it against a board

finding: fonts is isolated because it is UNFINISHED and then SUPERSEDED, and its isolation is structural: FontManager extends its own EventEmitter and emits on that private bus, so no composer.on() subscription can ever reach it — and no code calls any of its methods.
evidence: FontManager.ts:46 `export class FontManager extends EventEmitter`; every emit is `this.emit(...)` on that instance (:205, :209, :268, :274, :341, :374, :376, :471, :483) — not `this.composer.emit`. The constructor at :53 takes `_composer: Composer` and never uses it (underscore-prefixed). `grep -rn "composer.fonts" src demo` returns exactly one non-test hit, Composer.ts:1118 `if (this.fonts?.destroy) this.fonts.destroy()`. `git log --all -S "composer.fonts."` returns nothing — no method on it has ever been called.
fix: Wire it or delete it. 530 lines, a full test file, and a Composer slot exist for a manager that has only ever been constructed and destroyed.
chain: fonts -> Font -> any font operation -> composer.fonts.* (never called) -> the whole editor -> FontManager is constructed on every session and does nothing but register six system fonts into a Map nobody reads

finding: Uploading a custom font is a dead end with a lie at the end of it: the media library accepts .ttf/.otf/.woff/.woff2, then tells the user to apply it in 'Inspector → Font → My Fonts' — a group that does not exist in the font picker.
evidence: LibraryManager.tsx:462 `accept="image/*,video/*,audio/*,.svg,.ttf,.otf,.woff,.woff2"`. useMediaState.ts:214-218: `if (asset.type === "font" || asset.type === "fnt") { showToast("To use this font: select text on canvas → Inspector → Font → My Fonts", "info"); … return; }`. FontPicker.tsx builds its list from `SYSTEM_FONTS` and `GoogleFontsService.getInstance()` (:56, :59-65) — grep for 'My Fonts|myFonts|custom' across src/editor/inspector/sections/typography/*.tsx returns nothing. FontManager.uploadFont (FontManager.ts:291-344) is the code that would create that group, and it has no caller (MOD-D-18).
fix: Wire the media library's font assets into FontManager.uploadFont and add a 'My Fonts' group to FontPicker, or stop accepting font files in the uploader and remove the toast.
chain: fonts -> CustomFont -> upload a .woff2 to the media library -> the toast's 'Inspector → Font → My Fonts' -> editor/inspector FontPicker -> the named destination does not exist; the uploaded font can never be applied to anything

finding: The other route for an uploaded font — dragging it from the media library onto text — silently produces invalid CSS: it sets font-family to the asset URL, and no @font-face is ever declared for it.
evidence: dragPayload.ts:27 maps `fnt` → MediaInsertType `"font"`; useDropExecution.ts:90 reads that type and :119 calls `composer.mediaOps.insertMediaAt(src, insertType, …)`; MediaCommandLayer.ts:192-201 handles `kind === "font-applied"`; ElementManager.ts:396-421 is the branch, and :409 is `el.setStyle("font-family", src)` where `src` is the asset URL. `font-family: https://…/Inter.woff2` is not a family name, and the only @font-face writer for uploads, FontManager.loadCustomFont (FontManager.ts:349-379, `new FontFace(font.family, url(...))` + `document.fonts.add`), is never called.
fix: Route the drop through FontManager.uploadFont/loadCustomFont so a real family name is registered, then set font-family to that name — not to the file URL.
chain: fonts -> CustomFont -> drag a font asset onto selected text -> ElementManager.insertMediaAt 'font' branch -> engine/styles -> the element gets font-family:<url>, the text does not change, and a success event (INSERT_SUCCEEDED) is emitted anyway

finding: Nothing fonts owns survives a reload, including uploaded custom fonts stored as data URLs: the registry is a private Map and ProjectData has no fonts field.
evidence: FontManager.ts:47-51 `fonts: Map<string, Font>`, `loadedFonts: Set<string>`, `googleFontsCache`. uploadFont converts files to data URLs in memory (:294-299) and stores the CustomFont only in that Map (:336). `toggleFavorite` (:467-473) mutates the in-memory object. grep for 'fonts|customFonts' in shared/types/project.ts returns nothing — ProjectData (:30-49) has no such field, and neither does ProjectSettings. destroy() clears everything (:524-529).
fix: If custom fonts ship, they need an entity in ProjectData (or the asset store) plus an @font-face emit in the export; a data-URL Map cannot outlive the tab.
chain: fonts -> CustomFont + favourites -> upload a font / favourite a family -> reload -> ProjectData -> both are gone, and the published site would have had no @font-face for the upload either way

finding: FontManager is the only live-API Google Fonts path and it is dead; the shipping picker reads a static compiled-in catalogue, so the font list cannot change without a release.
evidence: FontManager.fetchGoogleFonts (:158-212) is the only `fetch` against `https://www.googleapis.com/webfonts/v1/webfonts` (:57) — unreachable per MOD-D-18. The live picker uses `GoogleFontsService`, whose list is `private fonts: GoogleFont[] = GOOGLE_FONT_CATALOGUE` (GoogleFontsService.ts:58) from shared/constants/googleFonts.ts, with no network call. The export's family whitelist reads the same constant (ExportHelpers.ts:135 `GOOGLE_FONT_CATALOGUE.filter(...)`).
fix: Fine as a deliberate choice — the export comment at ExportHelpers.ts:118-121 explains why the whitelist must be closed. Then delete fetchGoogleFonts, FONTS_GOOGLE_FETCHED and FONTS_GOOGLE_ERROR rather than leaving a second, live-network catalogue in the tree.
chain: fonts -> GoogleFont catalogue -> search for a family -> GoogleFontsService static array -> editor/inspector FontPicker -> a family Google added after the last build is unreachable, and FontManager's live fetch that would have it is dead

finding: All 7 FONT_* events are unreachable twice over — they fire on a private emitter that nothing subscribes to, from methods that are never called.
evidence: FONTS_GOOGLE_FETCHED (:205), FONTS_GOOGLE_ERROR (:209), FONT_LOADED (:268, :374), FONT_ERROR (:274, :376), FONT_UPLOADED (:341), FONT_FAVORITE_TOGGLED (:471), FONT_DELETED (:483) — all `this.emit` on FontManager's own EventEmitter. The only `.on()` against a FontManager instance in the repo is in its own test file (fonts/__tests__/FontManager.test.ts:62, :104).
fix: When the module is wired (MOD-D-19), FONT_LOADED should re-render the canvas so newly-loaded families paint, and FONT_ERROR should raise a toast — neither exists today.
chain: fonts -> Font.loaded -> load a Google or custom font -> FONT_LOADED -> editor/canvas + toast -> text that uses a still-loading family renders in the fallback with no repaint and no error when the load fails

finding: drag's isolation is NOMINAL in the event graph and REAL in the data flow, but the direction is the opposite of what the graph suggests: the canvas calls DragManager by direct method four times and reads it back zero times, so it is a write-only mirror, not a source of truth.
evidence: Write call sites: useCanvasElementDrag.ts:361 `composer.canvas.drag?.start(...)`, useDropTargetResolver.ts:153 `.move(...)`, useDropExecution.ts:304 `.end(dropSucceeded)`, useCanvasDragDrop.ts:214 and :250 `.cancel(...)`. Read call sites: `grep -rn "drag.getOperation|drag.isDragging|drag.getPhase|drag.getTargetId" src demo` returns nothing outside engine/drag and tests. The real SSOT is React state — useDragSession.ts:83 `useDragSession()`, consumed at useCanvasDragDrop.ts:12-13 and by every drop helper. DragManager.ts:2-4 nevertheless calls itself 'SSOT for drag & drop operations'.
fix: Either make the canvas read drag state from the engine (delete useDragSession's duplicate fields) or delete DragManager and its 5 events. Two state machines for one gesture is the CLAUDE.md §3 duplication rule.
chain: drag -> DragOperation -> drag an element on the canvas -> composer.canvas.drag.start/move/end -> (no reader) -> the engine records a full drag state machine that influences nothing; the canvas answers every question from its own React session

finding: The mirror is incomplete as well as unread: only element drags started on the canvas call start(), so for every panel-sourced drag the state machine stays idle and DRAG_MOVE / DRAG_END / DROP_ZONE_DROP never fire.
evidence: start() has exactly one call site, useCanvasElementDrag.ts:361, hard-coded to source `"canvas"`. move() returns immediately when `!this.operation` (DragManager.ts:101), end() likewise (:133), cancel() likewise (:156) — and the shared drop pipeline that calls them (useDropTargetResolver.ts:153, useDropExecution.ts:304) serves Insert, Layers, Media and Templates drags too. The `DragSource` union declares `"canvas" | "panel" | "external"` (drag/types.ts:42) and the last two values are never passed anywhere.
fix: Call start() from the panel drag sources (dragPayload.ts's setMediaDragData is the shared entry point) with source 'panel', or drop the unused union members and document the manager as canvas-element-only.
chain: drag -> DragOperation -> drag a block from the Insert panel onto the canvas -> start() is never called -> DragManager -> the drop lands correctly but the engine emits no DRAG_START/END and DROP_ZONE_DROP never fires for the most common drag in the product

finding: DRAG_CANCEL carries a reason string that no user ever sees, while the invalid-drop reason the user needs is held in React state that the engine has no access to.
evidence: DragManager.cancel(reason?) builds `DragCancelPayload { sessionId, reason }` (:158-161) and emits DRAG_CANCEL (:166); the two live callers pass "Left canvas" (useCanvasDragDrop.ts:214) and "Global dragend" (:250). Separately the canvas computes a real user-facing reason and keeps it locally: `session.setInvalidDropReason(validation.reason)` (useDropTargetResolver.ts:145). No listener exists for DRAG_CANCEL.
fix: Pass the validation reason into cancel() and let a toast or the drop affordance subscribe, so 'you cannot put a section inside a button' survives past the gesture.
chain: drag -> DragCancelPayload.reason -> drop on an invalid target -> DRAG_CANCEL -> editor/shell toasts -> the reason is discarded; the drag just snaps back with no explanation

finding: drag persists nothing, which is correct — DragOperation is a per-gesture value and is explicitly torn down — but it means the module contributes no entity to ProjectData and none of its 5 events can carry durable state.
evidence: DragManager.ts:45 `private operation: DragOperation | null = null`; cleared at end() (:142) and cancel() (:163); destroy() cancels any live one (:200-204) and is called from Composer.ts:1125. DragOperation (drag/types.ts:20-39) is not referenced in shared/types/project.ts.
fix: None needed — record it so the persistence question is answered explicitly for this module rather than left open.
chain: drag -> DragOperation -> any drag -> end/cancel -> (no store) -> correct by design: nothing should survive the gesture

finding: The single-drag invariant the class documents cannot hold across sources: because panel drags never register, a canvas drag and a panel drag can be live at once without the auto-cancel at start() ever running.
evidence: DragManager.ts:36-42 states invariants 1-3 ('Only ONE drag operation active at any time'); start() enforces it by auto-cancelling a stale operation (:62-65). That enforcement only runs on the one path that calls start() (MOD-D-25), so a panel drag begun while a canvas drag is pending leaves `this.operation` pointing at the canvas drag while the panel drop executes through useDropExecution.
fix: Same fix as MOD-D-25: register every drag source, or stop claiming the invariant in the class doc.
chain: drag -> DragOperation -> begin a panel drag during a pending canvas drag -> start() (not called for panels) -> DragManager -> the stale canvas operation is never auto-cancelled and end(success) attributes the panel drop to it

finding: templates is isolated because its wiring was REMOVED, and the removal is documented at both ends: the class was soft-deprecated 2026-05-07 and its last consumer, the TemplateLibrary modal, was retired 2026-07-25 — leaving a 477-line manager and a 129-line hook with zero callers.
evidence: TemplateManager.ts:1 `@deprecated DEAD/SIMULATED — soft-deprecated 2026-05-07 … do not build on this`, and :11-27 name the surviving consumer as 'useTemplateManager hook → src/templates/TemplateLibrary.tsx (and StudioModals)'. src/templates/index.ts:5-8 records the retirement: 'TemplateLibrary modal + SectionTemplates quick-inserts retired 2026-07-25'. `grep -rn "useTemplateManager" src demo` now returns only the hook itself and two barrel re-exports (editor/shell/index.ts:24, editor/shell/hooks/index.ts:25). engine/AGENTS.md:23 repeats the rule.
fix: Execute the deletion the deprecation note promised ('When the unification arc lands, this class is deleted in one PR'): remove TemplateManager, useTemplateManager, and the 8 TEMPLATE_* constants it owns.
chain: templates -> Template -> browse/apply a template -> useTemplateManager (no caller since 2026-07-25) -> engine/templates -> the engine store is superseded; every live template action goes through a different path

finding: The engine template store is superseded, not merely unused: the live save path writes localStorage and mirrors to the server without ever touching composer.templates, so the two stores can never agree.
evidence: Live save: useStudioHandlers.ts:94-149 `handleSaveTemplate` exports HTML (:97), runs inverseResolveTokens (:112), writes `localStorage[STORAGE_KEYS.MY_TEMPLATES]` (:121-124) and calls `mirrorUserTemplate(newTemplate)` (:144) → services/templateSync.ts:99-110 `userTemplates.upsert.mutate`. It is reached from AquibraStudio.tsx:649 → StudioModals.tsx:162. The engine's own saveAsTemplate (TemplateManager.ts:319-350) writes `this.templates.set(template.id, template)` (:343) into a private Map and emits TEMPLATE_SAVED (:345) — never called. Reads follow the same split: templatesData.ts:85 `getMyTemplates()` reads the localStorage key.
fix: Delete saveAsTemplate/loadTemplate/mergeTemplate/deleteTemplate/importTemplates with the class; the localStorage+server pair is the shipped contract.
chain: templates -> Template -> 'Save as Template' -> useStudioHandlers.handleSaveTemplate -> localStorage MY_TEMPLATES + templateSync -> composer.templates never learns the template exists, so its fetchTemplates() 'local' source is permanently empty

finding: The engine store persists nothing; the live store persists twice. Neither is in ProjectData, so 'my templates' is workspace state, not project state — worth stating because the two behave differently on reload.
evidence: Engine: TemplateManager.ts:51-53 `templates: Map`, `sources: TemplateSource[]`, `cache: Map` with a 5-minute TTL (:54); destroy() clears all three (:471-476, `destroy(): void` at :471). Live: localStorage under STORAGE_KEYS.MY_TEMPLATES (useStudioHandlers.ts:124) plus server rows via userTemplates.upsert (templateSync.ts:103-110), hydrated back with a three-state status machine (templateSync.ts:44-62 `TemplateHydrateState`). ProjectData (shared/types/project.ts:30-49) contains no templates field.
fix: None for the live path — it is correct. Record it so nobody re-adds a project-scoped template field.
chain: templates -> Template -> save a template -> reload -> localStorage + server userTemplates -> the live path survives and the engine Map does not, which is why the engine store is invisible even to its own fetchTemplates

finding: All 8 TEMPLATE_* events the engine owns fire on TemplateManager's PRIVATE emitter, not the composer bus — so even if the class had callers, no composer.on() subscription could hear them. The two template events that DO work (TEMPLATE_APPLIED, TEMPLATE_REMOVED) belong to the live panel path instead.
evidence: TemplateManager.ts:49 `extends EventEmitter`; emits are `this.emit(...)` at :71 (TEMPLATE_SOURCE_REGISTERED), :251+:271 (TEMPLATE_LOADING/TEMPLATE_LOADED), :278 (TEMPLATE_ERROR), :345 (TEMPLATE_SAVED), :405 (TEMPLATE_DELETED), :433 (TEMPLATE_CACHE_CLEARED), :464 (TEMPLATES_IMPORTED). The dead hook subscribed on that private bus with raw strings (useTemplateManager.ts:48-50 `composer.templates.on("template:saved", …)`). By contrast EVENT-GRAPH.json lists TEMPLATE_APPLIED and TEMPLATE_REMOVED as non-orphans, mentioned by ['engine:elements','panel:templates'].
fix: Delete the 8 constants with the class. Do not 'fix' them by re-pointing at composer.emit — that would create a second live template event set beside TEMPLATE_APPLIED/_REMOVED.
chain: templates -> Template -> apply a template -> TEMPLATE_LOADED on a private emitter -> panel:templates / editor:shell -> unreachable by construction; the live panel uses TEMPLATE_APPLIED on the shared bus instead

finding: loadTemplate's default and 'replace' branches both call composer.importProject(), which is the known-hollow path — it emits only PROJECT_LOADED, so undo/redo and restore never fire for a template apply.
evidence: TemplateManager.ts:255-263: `if (options.replace) { this.composer.importProject(template.data) }` (:255,:257) `… else { this.composer.importProject(template.data) }` (:263); mergeTemplate ends the same way (:313). This is the documented importProject shape (memory: importProject emits only PROJECT_LOADED).
fix: Moot if the class is deleted (MOD-D-29). If any of it is kept, route through the elements/importHTMLToActivePage path the live panel uses, which is transaction-aware.
chain: templates -> ProjectData -> apply a template with replace -> composer.importProject -> engine/HistoryManager -> the whole project is swapped with no undo entry, so Cmd+Z cannot get the previous site back

finding: Already filed, not re-filed: W-F-26 (template category pills filter on a field every template contradicts, so the gallery returns empty). Adding the module's view: that bug is on the LIVE panel path, which confirms the engine store is not merely unused but irrelevant — a category filter fix would not touch TemplateManager.applyFilters at all.
evidence: W-F-26 (findings/W-F.jsonl, Critical, Templates · gallery). The engine has its own complete, unreachable filter implementation for the same job: TemplateManager.applyFilters (:148-215) covers category, tags, query, freeOnly, minRating and four sort keys.
fix: Fix W-F-26 on the panel. Do not revive applyFilters for it.
chain: templates -> TemplateFilter -> filter the gallery by category -> the panel's own filter (broken per W-F-26) -> panel:templates -> the engine's parallel, working applyFilters is not consulted, because nothing can reach it

finding: CORRECTION to the premise: collaboration is NOT isolated. It is the most directly-wired of the six modules — five live cross-module call sites — and its apparent isolation is an artefact of the graph scanner searching for EVENTS.* constant names while the three real listeners subscribe with raw string literals.
evidence: Cross-module callers: HistoryManager.ts:243 `this.composer.collab?.manager` in recordAndMaybeBroadcast and :323 in recordForCollaboration; Composer.ts:352 `this.collab.manager.on("operation:apply", operationApplyHandler)` and :355-372 selection mirroring; StudioHeader.tsx:533 `composer.collab.manager.startSession(...)`; RemoteCursorsOverlay.tsx:118 + :149-150 `collab.on("cursor:update", …)` / `collab.on("user:leave", …)`. Those literals ARE the constants: events.ts:253 COLLAB_OPERATION_APPLY:"operation:apply", :246 COLLAB_CURSOR_UPDATE:"cursor:update", :244 COLLAB_USER_LEAVE:"user:leave".
fix: Re-point the three subscribers at the EVENTS constants so the graph stops mis-reporting them, and correct the orphan count: 20 genuine orphans, not 23.
chain: collaboration -> CollaborationEvent -> a peer moves their cursor -> COLLAB_CURSOR_UPDATE (subscribed as the literal "cursor:update") -> editor/canvas RemoteCursorsOverlay -> works today; the graph reports it as an orphan because the constant name never appears at the listener

finding: Of the 23 COLLAB_*/OT_* events, 3 are live and 20 are genuinely unconsumed — and the 20 are a GATED feature's unbuilt UI, not dead weight: locks, editing indicators, sync status and OT divergence are all emitted and all undrawn.
evidence: Live 3: operation:apply (Composer.ts:352), cursor:update + user:leave (RemoteCursorsOverlay.tsx:149-150). Unconsumed 20, all emitted: COLLAB_ROOM_CREATED (:138), ROOM_LEFT (:220), EDITING_UPDATE (:311, :674), EDITING_CLEARED (:342, :638, :767), LOCK_ACQUIRED (:375, :696), LOCK_RELEASED (:395, :699, :717, :773), LOCK_EXPIRED (:471), USER_JOIN (:607), SELECTION_UPDATE (:657), SYNC_ERROR (:749), SYNC_COMPLETE (:759), CONNECTION_LOST (:777), CONNECTION_RESTORED (:782), STATE_CHANGE (:792); plus OTEngine.ts OT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT (:83), OT_PENDING_CLEANUP (:91), OT_DIVERGENCE_DETECTED (:144), OT_OPERATION_PENDING (:189), OT_OPERATION_ACKED (:224), OT_OPERATION_TRANSFORMED (:247). The feature is gated: isFeatureEnabled("collab") at StudioHeader.tsx:225 (used at :759, :833) and useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:326.
fix: Keep them — they are the wire for the six known OT bugs' eventual UI. But COLLAB_SYNC_ERROR and OT_DIVERGENCE_DETECTED should get listeners BEFORE the flag is ever turned on: a non-convergence today is silent.
chain: collaboration -> OTOperation -> two peers edit the same element -> OT_DIVERGENCE_DETECTED -> (no listener) -> editor/shell -> the session diverges with no banner, no reload prompt and no telemetry — the exact failure mode the 6 known P1 bugs produce

finding: The flag gates the DOOR but not the ENGINE: CollaborationManager starts a 10-second setInterval in its constructor for every editor session, including every session with NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_COLLAB off, and RemoteCursorsOverlay mounts and subscribes with no flag check.
evidence: CollaborationManager.ts:80 `this.startCleanupInterval()` runs inside the constructor (:76-81); :86-91 sets `setInterval(..., CollaborationManager.CLEANUP_INTERVAL)` with CLEANUP_INTERVAL = 10000 (:72). The manager is constructed unconditionally at Composer.ts:277 `manager: new CollaborationManager(this)`. RemoteCursorsOverlay is rendered unconditionally at CanvasOverlayGroup.tsx:390 `<RemoteCursorsOverlay composer={composer} />` — no isFeatureEnabled("collab") guard, unlike StudioHeader.tsx:833. CLAUDE.md §No hidden side effects: 'Constructors and top-level const must be side-effect-free.'
fix: Move startCleanupInterval() into joinRoom/startSession and stop it on leaveRoom; gate the overlay on the flag like the header does.
chain: collaboration -> cleanup timer -> open the editor with collab OFF -> CollaborationManager constructor -> every editor session -> a 10s timer runs forever over two empty Maps, and a cursor overlay subscribes to a manager that will never connect

finding: Collaboration's local entities are all ephemeral by design; the only durable state is the server-side op log the SSE transport replays, and the room id is the site id — so a room cannot be named, listed or ended from the editor.
evidence: In-memory only: `room` (CollaborationManager.ts:58), `currentUser` (:59), `editingStates: Map` (:64), `elementLocks: Map` (:68); leaveRoom nulls the first two and clears editingStates (:214-218, clear at :217). Durable: SSETransport POSTs each event to `/api/collab/:roomId/ops` and replays from `/api/sse/collab/:roomId?since=:seq` (SSETransport.ts:4-6, :42). startSession passes the siteId straight through as the room id: `async startSession(siteId, userName) { … await this.joinRoom(siteId, userName) }` (:193-196).
fix: None while the flag is off. When it is considered, the site-id-as-room-id choice means every collaborator on a site shares one permanent room with no way to close it.
chain: collaboration -> CollaborationRoom -> start a session -> startSession(siteId) -> server op log at /api/collab/:siteId/ops -> the room is the site and is permanent; leaving only disconnects this client

finding: Element locks are computed, tracked, auto-expired and emitted — and drawn nowhere, so the module's whole conflict-prevention layer is invisible.
evidence: CollaborationManager maintains `elementLocks: Map<string, ElementLock>` (:68) with a 5s LOCK_TIMEOUT (:70), emits COLLAB_LOCK_ACQUIRED (:375, :696), COLLAB_LOCK_RELEASED (:395, :699, :717, :773) and COLLAB_LOCK_EXPIRED (:471), and sweeps stale locks every 10s (:86-91 → cleanupStaleLocks). None of the three has a listener anywhere in src/. The same is true of COLLAB_EDITING_UPDATE (:311, :674) and COLLAB_EDITING_CLEARED (:342, :638, :767) with their 3s EDITING_TIMEOUT (:66).
fix: Before the flag is enabled, subscribe the canvas selection ring and the Layers rows to LOCK_ACQUIRED/RELEASED/EXPIRED and EDITING_UPDATE — a soft lock nobody can see is a lock that does not exist.
chain: collaboration -> ElementLock -> a peer starts editing an element -> COLLAB_LOCK_ACQUIRED -> editor/canvas selection + panel:layers -> no lock badge, no dimming, no 'X is editing' — two people edit the same element and last write wins silently

finding: Connection state has no surface: COLLAB_STATE_CHANGE, COLLAB_CONNECTION_LOST, COLLAB_CONNECTION_RESTORED and COLLAB_SYNC_ERROR all fire with no listener, while the header's collaboration chip derives its state from a prop rather than from these events.
evidence: setState emits COLLAB_STATE_CHANGE (:792); connection handlers emit CONNECTION_LOST (:777) and CONNECTION_RESTORED (:782); a failed ProjectDataSchema parse emits COLLAB_SYNC_ERROR (:749). No `.on("state:change"|"connection:lost"|"connection:restored"|"sync:error")` exists in src/. StudioHeader reads `collaborationState !== "disconnected"` from a prop (:759) and `isConnected` (:833), so nothing re-renders when the transport actually drops — EventSource auto-reconnects behind the scenes (SSETransport.ts:67-70).
fix: Subscribe the header chip to COLLAB_STATE_CHANGE so 'connected' means the transport is connected, not that startSession once resolved.
chain: collaboration -> CollaborationState -> the SSE connection drops mid-session -> COLLAB_CONNECTION_LOST -> editor/shell StudioHeader -> the presence chip keeps reading 'connected' while the user's edits reach nobody

finding: Already filed, not re-filed: SH-A-20 and SH-B-14 (Presence is never drawn — all 105 topbar instances use the empty solo variant, including the presence board itself). Adding the module's view: this is consistent, not an oversight, because presence is the one collab surface that IS wired, so the gap is purely on the design side.
evidence: SH-A-20 (findings/SHELL-A.jsonl, Minor), SH-B-14 (findings/SHELL-B.jsonl, Major). Code side: PresenceIndicators.tsx:59 with `toPresenceUsers` imported at StudioHeader.tsx:30, driven by the live manager. RemoteCursorsOverlay.tsx:109-172 is likewise complete and mounted (CanvasOverlayGroup.tsx:390).
fix: Draw the multi-user presence variant, or accept that the collab flag stays off and mark the boards as deferred rather than leaving them empty.
chain: collaboration -> CollaborationUser -> a peer joins -> COLLAB_USER_JOIN -> editor/shell PresenceIndicators -> the code path works and no board draws its output, so the one shipped collab surface cannot be reviewed

finding: Three of the six modules emit onto a PRIVATE EventEmitter rather than the composer bus, which is the mechanical cause of most of their apparent isolation — composer.on() can never reach them regardless of how well their consumers are written.
evidence: Private-bus emitters (class extends EventEmitter, emits are `this.emit`): FontManager.ts:46, TemplateManager.ts:49, CollaborationManager.ts:55. Shared-bus emitters (`this.composer.emit`): FormHandler.ts:125 etc., InteractionManager.ts:51 etc., DragManager.ts:88 etc. Composer forwards exactly one private event onto anything: Composer.ts:352 subscribes `collab.manager.on("operation:apply", …)` — there is no general re-broadcast.
fix: Pick one convention. If private buses stay, the event graph must resolve `<instance>.on(...)` as well as `composer.on(...)`, and events.ts should mark which bus each constant belongs to — 22 of the 58 orphans in these six modules are private-bus by construction and can never have a composer listener.
chain: cross-module -> EVENTS constants -> emit from a manager -> the manager's own EventEmitter -> any composer.on() subscriber -> the subscription silently never fires, and the event graph reports the event as an orphan

finding: Answering the pass's question directly: of the six 'fully isolated' modules, only THREE should be connected and are not (forms, fonts, interactions). One is correctly self-contained (drag, by gesture scope). One should be DELETED rather than connected (templates). One is already connected and was mis-measured (collaboration).
evidence: Wiring style per module — forms: shared bus + direct call, both surfaces unmounted (MOD-D-01). interactions: shared bus, bypassed by a duplicate direct-call writer (MOD-D-10). fonts: private bus, zero callers ever (MOD-D-18). drag: shared bus, 4 direct write calls / 0 reads (MOD-D-24). templates: private bus, consumer retired 2026-07-25 (MOD-D-29). collaboration: private bus with 3 literal-string subscribers + 5 direct call sites across HistoryManager, Composer, StudioHeader and the canvas overlay (MOD-D-35).
fix: Treat them as three different jobs, not one: mount two surfaces (forms, fonts), de-duplicate one writer (interactions), delete one class (templates), correct one measurement (collaboration), and decide whether drag's engine mirror earns its place at all.
chain: cross-module -> module wiring -> the '6 fully isolated modules' measurement -> checking direct calls as well as events -> the dependency map -> 3 genuine gaps, 1 correct isolation, 1 deletion, 1 false positive

finding: Persistence, stated explicitly for all six: fonts and templates(engine) lose everything on reload; forms loses everything except the one field written by an unmounted component; interactions and collaboration persist correctly; drag correctly persists nothing.
evidence: NOT persisted — FontManager.ts:47-51 (Map/Set, cleared at :524-529) with no fonts field in shared/types/project.ts:30-49; TemplateManager.ts:51-53 (Map, cleared at :471-476); FormHandler.ts:104-106 + FormSubmissionService.ts:99. PERSISTED — interactions at element.data.data.interactions, which rides ElementData.data (shared/types/element.ts:76) inside ProjectData.pages (project.ts:34); collaboration ops server-side via SSETransport.ts:4-6. CORRECTLY EPHEMERAL — DragManager.ts:45. PARTIAL — element.data.formConfig persists but has only the unmounted writer (FormSettingsSection.tsx:45).
fix: For fonts, custom fonts need a real entity (asset store or ProjectData) plus an export-side @font-face before the upload path is wired — otherwise MOD-D-19's fix produces a font that works until reload.
chain: cross-module -> module entities -> author anything in fonts or engine-templates -> reload -> ProjectData -> the work is gone, because neither module has a field in the project snapshot or a sync service of its own
